```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  collapse = TRUE,

  message = FALSE,

  fig.height = 6
)
```

This article shows how to call from R the same analysis you access in jamovi's interface. The code on this page runs each time the site is built.

```{r setup}
library(jsurvival)
```

```{r data-histopathology}
data("histopathology", package = "jsurvival")
```

```{r glimpse-histopathology}
dplyr::glimpse(histopathology[, c("SurgeryDate", "LastFollowUpDate", "OverallTime", "Outcome", "LVI")])
```

# Run the analysis

The options `dod`, `dooc`, `awd` and `awod` are required arguments. Pass `NULL` for them unless you use multiple event levels. `outcomeLevel` is the value of the outcome column that means the event happened. Here survival time is calculated from the two date columns.

```{r survival-analysis}
overall_survival <- jsurvival::survival(
    data = histopathology,
    elapsedtime = "OverallTime",
    tint = TRUE,
    dxdate = "SurgeryDate",
    fudate = "LastFollowUpDate",
    explanatory = "LVI",
    outcome = "Outcome",
    outcomeLevel = "1",
    dod = NULL,
    dooc = NULL,
    awd = NULL,
    awod = NULL,
    timetypedata = "ymdhms",
    sc = TRUE,
    ce = TRUE,
    ch = TRUE
    )
```

# Read the results

The result is a list of the items you see in jamovi.

```{r item-names}
overall_survival$itemNames
```

```{r subtitle}
overall_survival$subtitle
```

## Median survival

```{r median-table}
overall_survival$medianTable
```

```{r median-summary}
overall_survival$medianSummary
```

## Cox regression

```{r cox-table}
overall_survival$coxTable
```

A table can be read as a data frame:

```{r cox-table-df}
overall_survival$coxTable$asDF
```

```{r cox-summary}
overall_survival$coxSummary
```

## Survival at selected times

```{r surv-table}
overall_survival$survTable
```

```{r surv-summary}
overall_survival$survTableSummary
```

# Plots

Survival plot:

```{r plot-survival}
overall_survival$plot
```

Cumulative events:

```{r plot-events}
overall_survival$plot2
```

Cumulative hazard:

```{r plot-hazard}
overall_survival$plot3
```

To save a plot as a PNG file:

```{r save-plot}
png_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
overall_survival$plot$saveAs(png_file)
file.exists(png_file)
```

# Notes

- Keep event coding and time units consistent with your dataset.
- These results describe associations in the data. They do not establish causes.
